proposed_english: the unique one / the only one
rationale: Lycopolitan substantival form related to ⲥⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'single, unique, alone.' Used here as title 'the unique upholder/chief of all the omophoroi.'
ⲛⲁⲃ = ⲛⲟϭ ('great') + ⲕⲱⲧ ('builder, mason'). Title for the Living Spirit as cosmic architect who fashioned the universe — Manichaean cosmogonic role. Distinct from ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲧⲏⲥ (the dark molder).
Greek loanword ὠμοφόρος (shoulder-bearer, Atlas). The plural 'Omophoroi' designates the cosmic Bearers — multiple figures of the Atlas/Pillar-of-Glory class. Preserved as Greek technical term.

Compound ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲃⲱⲗ ('release/loose'). The agent-noun for the cosmic figure who releases bound light/souls. Standard formation parallel to ⲣⲉϥ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher,' ⲡⲣⲉϩⲛⲉⲥⲥⲉ 'awakener,' ⲡⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲩⲥ 'gatherer.'
Compound ⲣⲉϥ- + ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ ('to wake'). Title of the Mind of Light as one who awakens the sleeping souls. Ennoetic-soteriological function.
Compound ⲣⲉϥ- + ⲥⲱⲟⲩϩⲥ ('to gather'). Title of the Mind of Light as one who reassembles the scattered light-particles into recognition.
Lycopolitan reduplicated form related to ϣⲣ̄ⲣ̄ 'scatter, disperse.' Used of the dispersed light-souls awaiting reassembly.
Lycopolitan plural of ⲉⲓⲁ/ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye,' written ⲛ̄ⲓⲁⲧⲉ. Preserved as 'the eyes' in correspondential register (eyes of light = organs of recognition).

Coptic abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- ('state-of') + Greek ⲡⲁⲣⲁ- ('alongside, contrary') + ⲡⲉⲥⲟⲩⲧ (= ⲥⲟⲩⲧⲱⲛ 'straight, upright'). 'State-of-being-aside-from-the-straight' = doctrinal deviance. Used here of the heretics' system.
Adjectival/nominal base of ⲙⲛⲧⲡⲁⲣⲁⲡⲉⲥⲟⲩⲧ. ⲡⲁⲣⲁ- (Gk 'beside') + ⲡⲉⲥⲟⲩⲧ ('the straight') = 'aside-the-straight,' crooked, deviant.
Greek καθάριος. Sect-name self-designation of the Baptists discussed in this chapter. Manichaean polemic identifies their five sayings.
Privative ⲁⲧ- + ϯ-ⲣⲉⲛ ('to give a name,' Lyc. ⲣⲉⲛ/ⲡⲉⲛ) + ⲁⲣⲁϩ ('to him') = 'the one to whom no name is given.' Apophatic title of the Father in the Baptists' first saying.
Lycopolitan with prosthetic ⲧ- of Greek πάλιν. Standard dialogue-introducing adverb in Kephalaia.
